title: Cuban Nationalists
capsule: The Cuban Nationalists designates the independence movement launched on 24 February 1895 with the Grito de Baire under the Cuban Revolutionary Party, whose ideological founder José Martí was killed at Dos Ríos on 19 May 1895. Generals Máximo Gómez and Antonio Maceo prosecuted a devastating westward march, burning sugar estates to deny Spain colonial revenue, until Maceo's death in December 1896. U.S. intervention following the explosion of the USS Maine in Havana harbor (February 1898) transformed the conflict into the Spanish-American War; Spain surrendered Cuba in the Treaty of Paris (December 1898) and the United States exercised military occupation until 1902, leaving the nationalists' goal of full sovereignty constrained by the Platt Amendment. The dataset's window of 1895–1900 covers the insurrection and the transitional occupation.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The military history is well documented; territorial control of nationalist forces fluctuated continuously across the island and does not map to stable bounded regions, making spatial attestation inherently approximate.
